## Restart (`outputs: - type: restart`, `-r` or `--restart`) {#sec-ch15-restart}

### Summary

A restart file is the saved state of a run: every variable each block holds, the time and cycle, the output
schedules, and, with anomaly storage, the reference the anomalies are measured from. A run resumes from it by
reading its own block's part, checking that the file was written for this grid and this state layout, restoring
the schedules by position and by key, and continuing from the saved time. The restart writer exists so that a
long run can be cut into legs, and the metadata checks exist so that a file written for another grid, another
precision or another storage form is refused instead of silently reinterpreted.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Saves each block's state and output schedule, bundles the blocks' parts into one file, and resumes a
run from that file at the saved time and cycle.

**Data.** Writes `<basename>.<NNNNN>.restart` (and `<basename>.final.restart` at the end of the run); on resume each
block reads its own part by rank.

**Placement.** `make_outputs` at the output's cadence and on the final call (write); `initialize` with a restart
path, before the first step (read).

**Activation.** `outputs: - type: restart` with `dt`; the driver's `-r <file>` (or `--restart`), or
`initialize_from_restart` from Python. Default: no restart output.

**Guarantee / limits.** The state is written in its own dtype on the host and read back bit for bit; a same-dtype
resume continues the run bit for bit; a file written with anomaly storage on is refused when it is for another
grid, another metadata version or another stored dtype; a file without the metadata pair is read as a legacy
file without those checks. A resume needs the same block decomposition.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of this section, @tbl-ch15-restart-tests.
:::

Local symbols of this section: $t_r$ the time saved in the file [s]; $t_{\mathrm{next}}$ an output's saved next time
[s]; $\Delta t_o$ its interval [s]; $N$ the number of outputs of the deck. *Aliases.* Lane O's item O7 (the merged
writer, bundle and reader) in commit messages.

### Derivation

None: the section describes a file format and a resume protocol. Four invariants take the place of a derivation;
each is a statement about the code at the pin, and the Tests layer names the test that holds it.

1. *What is saved is the state, in its own dtype.* Every defined entry of the block's variables goes to the file
   on the host, except the scalar primitives when the scalar conserved state is present (they are rebuilt), and
   except a budget carry read from an earlier restart, in `RestartOutput::write_output_file`
   ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp RestartOutput::write_output_file >}}). With anomaly storage the file also
   holds the totals as `hydro_u`, the stored anomalies as `hydro_u_stored`, the reference `hydro_ref`, a metadata
   pair `[1, bits]` with the stored dtype's width, the three face coordinates the reference was built on, the
   species reference, and the solid fill values as totals; the names are `kHydroRestartMetadata`
   ({{< code src/output/restart_metadata.hpp kHydroRestartMetadata >}}) and `kHydroReferenceGrid`
   ({{< code src/output/restart_metadata.hpp kHydroReferenceGrid >}}).
2. *A same-dtype resume is exact.* The totals are float64 and the anomalies keep their stored bits, so reading
   `hydro_u_stored` back gives the same state the run had; stepping on from it gives the same bits as the
   uninterrupted run, which `precision_cases` ({{< code tests/test_fp32_restart.py precision_cases >}}) checks.
   A cross-precision resume rebuilds the state in the target dtype from the totals and is bounded by the test,
   not exact.
3. *The schedule is saved as advanced.* `make_outputs` advances an output's schedule only after writing it
   (@eq-ch15-output-schedule). A restart written in the same pass therefore saves, for itself and for every
   output after it that fires at this time, the file number and next time *as they will be after the pass*, so a
   resumed run does not write the source restart or the other outputs' frames again; this is the schedule loop
   of `RestartOutput::write_output_file` ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp RestartOutput::write_output_file >}}),
   and `test_restart_resume_schedule.py` ({{< code tests/test_restart_resume_schedule.py >}}) states it as its
   docstring. The saved schedules are keyed, legacy keys first and exact keys after them; the keys are
   `OutputType::schedule_key` ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::schedule_key >}}) and
   `OutputType::schedule_key_v2` ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::schedule_key_v2 >}}).
4. *A file that carries the metadata pair is refused unless it fits this block.* `check_restart_metadata`
   ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp check_restart_metadata >}}) runs its checks only when the file holds
   `kHydroRestartMetadata`, which a run with anomaly storage on writes: then the metadata version must be 1;
   `hydro_ref` and `hydro_u_stored` must be present; the stored dtype and shape must match the metadata and
   the totals; and the three saved face coordinates must equal this block's, bit for bit. A file without the
   pair, written by a run without anomaly storage, passes without those checks (the legacy arm of the test
   below). Independently of the pair, a `perturbation-flux` run needs the original `hydro_ref` and
   `hydro_ref_species`. A truncated bundle, a bundle without this
   block's part, and a bundle with a broken index all throw in `load_restart`
   ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp load_restart >}}).

### Numerical method

**Write.** `RestartOutput::write_output_file` ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp RestartOutput::write_output_file >}})
gathers each block's variables on the host (invariant 1), adds `last_time` and `last_cycle`, then for every output
of the block its file number and next time, advanced when the output fires in this pass (invariant 3), the
outputs' carries (the budget interval; @sec-ch10), and the two key lists. It saves the map as a tensor archive
`<basename>.block<r>.<NNNNN>.part`, or `.final.part` on the final call. A restart output is always combined: its
constructor `RestartOutput::RestartOutput` ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp RestartOutput::RestartOutput >}})
sets `combine` on.

**Bundle.** `RestartOutput::combine_blocks` ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp RestartOutput::combine_blocks >}})
runs under the same per-process protocol as the gridded writers (`combine_on_root`,
{{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp combine_on_root >}}): the root collects the parts, removes a stale target,
renames a single part, or writes a bundle with `make_restart_bundle`
({{< code src/output/restart.cpp make_restart_bundle >}}): one magic line `SNAPY_RESTART_BUNDLE_V1`, the part
count, one `<part name>\t<bytes>` line per part, an empty line, then the parts' bytes in index order. The parts
are then removed. The result is `<output_dir>/<basename>.<NNNNN>.restart` or `<basename>.final.restart`.

**Read.** `load_restart` ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp load_restart >}}) reads a file whose first line is not
the magic as one block's archive, whole; for a bundle it parses the index, finds the entry whose part name carries
`block<rank>` of this block (`part_rank`, {{< code src/output/restart.cpp part_rank >}}), copies its bytes to a
temporary file, reads that as an archive and removes it. Python exposes the same reader as
`snapy.load_restart(path, rank)` in the module definition `PYBIND11_MODULE`
({{< code python/csrc/snapy.cpp PYBIND11_MODULE >}}).

**Resume.** `MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_restart.cpp MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart >}}) is entered through
`MeshBlockImpl::initialize` with a restart file ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize >}}),
the driver's `-r`/`--restart` argument (`ParseArguments`, {{< code examples/straka.cpp ParseArguments >}}) or
`initialize_from_restart` from Python (bound in `bind_mesh`, {{< code python/csrc/pymesh.cpp bind_mesh >}}):

1. A relative path that does not exist is looked up under `output_dir`; the block's part is read; `hydro_u`,
   `last_time`, `last_cycle`, `file_number` and `next_time` must be present; the metadata checks run
   (invariant 4).
2. The cycle and time are restored from the file, so a run limited by `nlim`[^rg-92bdb6d45d3b] takes no extra step.
3. The schedules are restored. When the file holds $2N$ keys the exact keys are used, else the legacy ones. An
   output that still matches its own saved slot keeps it; an output whose key matches an unclaimed slot takes
   that slot; an output with no match keeps its position when that slot is unclaimed. The file number always
   follows the position, because the file name is `out<n>`. The next time is the saved one, except that a saved
   time more than one interval past the resume is pulled to $t_r + \Delta t_o$ (a disabled output whose interval
   was shrunk would otherwise never fire), and a new output joins the grid at $t_r - (t_r \bmod \Delta t_o)$.
4. Each output loads its carry; the variables move to the block's device, the reference, metadata and carry
   entries staying out of the variable map.
5. With anomaly storage the file's reference is reused and the stored anomaly bits are taken as the state; a
   file without a reference can only resume a single-block run, which rebuilds the reference from the restored
   state at rest; the solid fill values are put in stored form too.
6. With `perturbation-flux` the state is stored by the precision policy; a radiating boundary needs its saved
   reference tensors; the timing entries are removed from the variables; the scalar primitives are rebuilt from
   the conserved scalars; and the block's state store is reallocated and its executor entry invalidated, so the
   next step adopts the new storage.

All six steps are the body of `MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_restart.cpp MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart >}}), in this order.

### Code

**How to use it.** Write a restart every 3600 s and resume the run from the second one:

```yaml
outputs:
  - type: restart
    dt: 3600.
  - type: netcdf
    dt: 600.
    variables: [prim]
```

```sh
straka.release deck.yaml                       # the base leg
straka.release deck.yaml -r deck.00002.restart  # resumes at the second restart's time
```

The resumed run continues the file numbers of every output from the saved schedule: with the deck above it writes
`out1` frames from the next unwritten number, not from zero.

**What is refused, and why.**

- A file with the metadata pair for another grid: "reference grid mismatch; remap totals and initialize a new
  background". A serialized reference must never be attached to a different grid of the same shape; the check
  is in `check_restart_metadata` ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp check_restart_metadata >}}).
- With the metadata pair: another metadata version, a stored dtype or shape that disagrees with the metadata,
  and a file with the pair but without `hydro_ref` and `hydro_u_stored`; with or without the pair, a
  `perturbation-flux` resume without the original references, also in `check_restart_metadata`
  ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp check_restart_metadata >}}). A file without the pair is not checked against
  the grid at all.
- A truncated or malformed bundle, and a bundle with no part for this block, in `load_restart`
  ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp load_restart >}}).
- A multi-block anomaly run resuming from a file written without `hydro_ref`, and a radiating-boundary run
  resuming from a file without its boundary references, in `MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart`
  ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_restart.cpp MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart >}}).

**The excerpt.** Invariant 4, the checks of `check_restart_metadata`
({{< code src/output/restart.cpp check_restart_metadata >}}):

```cpp
    TORCH_CHECK(meta[0].item<int64_t>() == kHydroRestartVersion,
                "restart: unsupported hydro restart metadata version");
    TORCH_CHECK(data.count("hydro_ref") && data.count("hydro_u_stored"),
                "restart: metadata requires hydro_ref and hydro_u_stored");
    auto const& stored = data.at("hydro_u_stored");
    int bits = stored.scalar_type() == torch::kFloat32   ? 32
               : stored.scalar_type() == torch::kFloat64 ? 64
                                                         : 0;
    TORCH_CHECK(bits && meta[1].item<int64_t>() == bits &&
                    stored.sizes() == data.at("hydro_u").sizes(),
                "restart: stored hydro dtype/shape disagrees with metadata");
    for (int d = 0; d < 3; ++d) {
      auto key = kHydroReferenceGrid[d];
      TORCH_CHECK(data.count(key) &&
                      torch::equal(data.at(key), grid[d].to(torch::kCPU)),
                  "restart: reference grid mismatch at ", key,
                  "; remap totals and initialize a new background");
    }
```

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- A resume needs the same block decomposition: the bundle holds one part per block rank and each block reads
  the part of its rank in `load_restart` ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp load_restart >}}); a different grid
  is refused by the face check when the file carries the metadata pair, a different number of blocks by the
  missing part.
- Only the block's variables are saved. Counters a block keeps outside its variable map, the EfStatus slots of
  @sec-ch08 and the register's monitor counts of @sec-ch10, are not in the file and start from the resume; the
  budget interval is the one exception, carried by `BudgetCarry` ({{< code src/output/restart.hpp BudgetCarry >}}).
- A multi-block anomaly run can only resume from a file that holds `hydro_ref`
  (`MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_restart.cpp MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart >}}).
- The schedule keys hash the type, the interval and the variable names; two outputs that agree on all three are
  distinguished by position only (`OutputType::schedule_key_v2`,
  {{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::schedule_key_v2 >}}).
- A cross-precision resume is not bit-exact; the state is rebuilt from the float64 totals in the target dtype,
  as `precision_cases` ({{< code tests/test_fp32_restart.py precision_cases >}}) bounds it.
- The restart writer always combines; a `combine: false` on a restart entry is overridden by
  `RestartOutput::RestartOutput` ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp RestartOutput::RestartOutput >}}).
:::
